newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't starts laying off state workers.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't starts laying off state workers.

text.p: The Argentine government has begun the planned lay-offs of 10,000 public employees in 1997 as part of reforms to streamline the public sector which were launched last year, officials said Tuesday.

"We estimate 10,000 people will join the retraining fund," an Economy Ministry official told Reuters. "We have already paid redundancy compensation to less than 2,000 people and the salaries of 4,000 more are being paid into the fund."

The fund was set up in 1996 to finance the lay-off and retraining of state workers. Those suspended are kept on pay and trained for a year. At the end of that year, if they have not found new jobs with the state, they are laid off.
The government of President Carlos Menem aims to reduce public expenditure by $550 million a year through lay-offs.

Officials from state workers' union ATE said they did not rule out industrial action to oppose the lay-offs, which are part of the so-called "Second Reform of State" launched by Menem's government in 1996.
